title: Fewer Heads, Fewer Memories: Pruning Redundant Attention Heads Suppresses Verbatim Memorisation
abstract: arXiv:2610.40974v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models have been shown to memorise and reproduce verbatim sequences from their training data, raising concerns about privacy leakage, intellectual property exposure, and the limits of generalisation. Recent theoretical work suggests that attention heads may contribute to this behaviour by functioning as associative memory mechanisms, with memorisation capacity scaling with the number of heads. At the same time, empirical work has shown that many attention heads are redundant and can be pruned with limited impact on downstream performance. Despite these parallel findings, the effect of pruning redundant heads on memorised-sequence reproduction remains unexplored. In this work, we demonstrate that zeroing out a substantial fraction of attention heads prior to inference can significantly suppress verbatim memorisation while preserving, or even improving, language modelling performance on the benchmark used to identify redunda

translated_title: 更少的注意力头，更少的记忆：剪枝冗余注意力头可抑制逐字记忆
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型已被证明能够记忆并逐字复现其训练数据中的序列，这引发了对隐私泄露、知识产权暴露以及泛化能力局限性的担忧。近期的理论研究表明，注意力头可能通过充当联想记忆机制而促成这种行为，其记忆容量会随注意力头数量的增加而扩展。与此同时，实证研究表明许多注意力头是冗余的，可以在对下游性能影响有限的情况下被剪枝。尽管有这些平行的发现，剪枝冗余注意力头对记忆序列复现的影响仍未被探索。在这项工作中，我们证明在推理之前将相当大比例的注意力头置零，可以显著抑制逐字记忆，同时在用于识别冗余注意力头的基准上保持甚至提升语言建模性能。
tldr: 本研究发现在推理前将大量冗余注意力头置零，可以在保持甚至提升语言建模性能的同时，显著抑制大语言模型对训练数据的逐字记忆复现。
en_tdlr: Zeroing out a substantial fraction of redundant attention heads before inference can significantly suppress verbatim memorisation of training data in large language models while preserving or even improving language modelling performance.
